rationale: P characterises the braking behaviour that T directly requires evaluating: whether a required braking maneuver occurs or is omitted. SG-1 and FR-7 establish braking itself as the subject of evaluation, rather than merely a control mechanism affecting another phenomenon. FR-7.1 supports including braking initiation. The obstacle-avoidance scope is supported by the hazard and the general braking requirement. P does not incorporate sensing, computation, communication, failure mitigation, or their timing constraints into the phenomenon.
determining_elements: “Whether braking is required” identifies the condition under which omission matters, consistent with SG-1.
“Started, performed, or omitted” characterises braking initiation and occurrence, supported by FR-7.1, FR-7, SG-1, and hazard H-1.
The scope covers driving situations involving obstacles or road users requiring collision-avoidance braking; FR-7 supports this broader scope beyond the hazard’s specific pedestrian scenario.
The stated phenomenon remains braking-maneuver behaviour and does not expand to the mechanisms used to detect obstacles or generate and communicate braking commands.
